title: Synchronization License (Composition)
summary: License a song's composition (music and lyrics) for use in timed relation with video: film, TV, ads, games or online video.
useWhen: A production wants to use a song. Pair it with a master use license if they will use the original recording, rather than a re-recording.
watchOuts: Every recorded song has two separate copyrights: the composition (music and lyrics), usually owned by songwriters and their publishers, and the sound recording or master, usually owned by whoever paid for or made the recording (the artist or label). Licenses and splits for one do not cover the other. A sync license covers only the composition. Using the original recording also needs a master use license from the master owner.

Every co-owner's share must be cleared, or the publisher must confirm it can license 100%. In the U.S., co-owners can often grant non-exclusive licenses for the whole song, but many productions require sign-off from every publisher.
Public performance (broadcast, streaming, theaters) is licensed separately through PROs. The production should file a cue sheet so writers get paid.
Changing the lyrics or making a parody usually needs separate approval.

variables.help: Songwriters (for the composition) or recording artist (for the master).

variables.label: Licensor's controlled share
variables.help: Percent of the rights the licensor controls. Other co-owners must license their shares separately.

variables.help: Film, episode, ad, game or video.

variables.help: How the music is used on screen.

variables.help: Fee increases to match the other side of the song if they get more.

variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 2. Composition
sections.body: Musical composition "{{song_title}}", written by {{writers_or_artist}} (the "Composition"). Every recorded song has two separate copyrights: the composition (music and lyrics), usually owned by songwriters and their publishers, and the sound recording or master, usually owned by whoever paid for or made the recording (the artist or label). Licenses and splits for one do not cover the other.

sections.title: 3. License
sections.body: On payment of {{fee}}, Licensor grants Licensee a non-exclusive license to record the Composition in synchronization with the Production, and to reproduce and distribute the Production with the Composition. Use: {{use_type}}, up to {{duration}} seconds in total, {{uses}} use(s), in the production "{{production}}" (the "Production"), in {{media}}, throughout {{territory}}, {{term}}. Licensor's controlled share: {{controlled_share}}%.

sections.title: 4. Not included
sections.body: Not included: the sound recording (master), which requires a separate master use license; public performance rights, which are licensed through performing rights organizations; use outside the Production; use in a soundtrack album; and any change to the lyrics or the fundamental character of the music without Licensor's written approval.

sections.title: 5. Cue sheet
sections.body: Licensee will prepare an accurate cue sheet listing the Composition, writers, publishers, PRO affiliations, timing and use, file it with the relevant PROs or require its distributor or broadcaster to do so, and send Licensor a copy within 30 days after the first broadcast or release.

sections.title: 7. Most-favored-nations
sections.body: If Licensee pays the owner of the master recording, or any other owner of the Composition, a higher fee or better terms for the same use, Licensor's fee and terms will be increased to match.

sections.title: 8. Licensor's promises
sections.body: Licensor controls {{controlled_share}}% of the Composition and has the right to grant this license for that share. Licensor will indemnify Licensee against claims that the licensed share infringes another's rights, up to the fee paid.

sections.title: 9. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
